newsitem.title: UK: Braemar reports Indian tanker scrapping nerves.
newsitem.headline: Braemar reports Indian tanker scrapping nerves.

text.p: London shipbroker Braemar reported the demolition sale of a VLCC to Bangladesh breakers amid reports of nervousness in the Indian ship scrapping market after the introduction of new safety rules.
Braemar said the 317,588 dwt Liotina, built in 1974, was sold in excess of $189 per light displacement tonne (ldt) to Bangladesh ship breakers last week.
It reported seven vessels sold to Indian breakers, of which four were general cargoships.
The only tanker was the 1971 built chemical carrier Stolt Llandaff, 25,233 dwt, which was reported sold at $220/ldt.
Braemar said recent weeks have seen a nervous change in the Indian market following the explosion of a tanker at Alang.
It said new safety guidelines had been introduced by the local authorities, which were seen by some in the industry as restrictive.
Braemar added that a budget announcement last week had also thrown the Bangladesh scrapping market into confusion as a result of a 100 percent increase in import duties.
